questions.question: A toy is in the form of a cone mounted on a hemisphere. The radius of the hemisphere and that of the cone is 7 cm and height of the cone is 5 cm. The total surface area of the toy (take π =22over7) is (rounded off to two places of decimal):
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Radius of the hemisphere = 7 cm

Radius of the cone = 7 cm

Height of the cone = 5 cm

**Concept:**

The total surface area of the toy = curved surface area of the cone + surface area of the hemisphere

**Calculation:**

Curved surface area of the cone = πrl (where l is the slant height)

⇒ Slant height, l = √(r² + h²) = √(7² + 5²) = √(49 + 25) = √(74)

⇒ Curved surface area of the cone = (22/7) × 7 × √(74)

Surface area of the hemisphere = 2πr²

⇒ Surface area of the hemisphere = 2 × (22/7) × 7²

Total surface area of the toy = curved surface area of the cone + surface area of the hemisphere

Total surface area of the toy = (22/7) × 7 × √(74) + 2 × (22/7) × 72

Total surface area of the toy = 22 × 8.602 + 2 × 22 × 7 = 497.25

**Therefore, rounding off to two places of decimal, the total surface area of the toy = 497.25 cm².**

questions.question: Find the mean proportional of (x + y)⁴ and (x - y)⁴.
questions.solution:
Mean proportional of (x + y)⁴ and (x - y)⁴

**Given values:**

(x + y)⁴ and (x - y)⁴

**Concept: **

The mean proportional of two quantities a and b is √(a × b) 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Mean proportional = √((x + y)⁴ × (x - y)⁴) = (x² - y²)²

**Therefore, the mean proportional of (x + y)⁴ and (x - y)⁴ is (x² - y²)²**

questions.question: The average salary of all the workers in a factory is Rs. 3,000. Among these workers, there are 12 higher officers and their average salary is Rs.12,000. The average salary of the remaining workers is Rs. 2,500. The total number of the workers is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Average salary of all workers = Rs. 3,000

Number of higher officers = 12

Average salary of higher officers = Rs. 12,000

Average salary of remaining workers = Rs. 2,500

**Concept: **

Total salary = Average salary × total number of individuals.

Also, total salary = salary of group A + salary of group B.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total salary of higher officers = number of higher officers × average salary of higher officers = 12 × 12,000

⇒ Let x be the total number of workers. Therefore, total salary of all workers = x × 3,000

⇒ Total salary of remaining workers = total salary of all workers - total salary of higher officers = x × 3,000 - 12 × 12,000

⇒ As total salary of remaining workers = (x - 12) × 2,500

⇒ (x - 12) × 2,500 = x × 3,000 - 12 × 12,000

⇒ 2500x - 30000 = x × 3,000 - 144,000

⇒ 500x = 114000

⇒ x = 228

**Hence, the total number of workers is 228.**

questions.question: The HCF of {3over8}, {5over12} and 15over16 is:
questions.solution:
**Given fractions: **3/8, 5/12, 15/16

**Concept: **

HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators/LCM of denominators

**Calculation:**

⇒ HCF of numerators (3, 5, 15) = 1

⇒ LCM of denominators (8, 12, 16) = 48

**Therefore, the HCF of the given fractions is 1/48.**

questions.question: A sum of money compound interest annually, the principal becomes Rs 30,250 in 2 years and Rs 33,275 in 3 years. Then find the principal?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time = 2 years

Amount = Rs. 30250

Time = 3 years

Amount = Rs. 33275

**Concept Used:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T

where, P = Principal

R = rate of interest

T = Time

**Calculation:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T

30250 = P(1 + R/100)² .....................(i)

When T = 3 years

33275 = P(1 + R/100)3 .....................(ii)

Divide equation (ii) by (i), we get

33275/30250 = (1 + R/100)

1331/1210 = (1 + R/100)

1 + 121/1210 = (1 + R/100)

R/100 = 121/1210

R/100 = 1/10

R = 10%

Put the value in equation(i)

30250 = P(1 + 10/100)2 

P = 30250 × 100/121

P = 25000

**Therefore, the sum is Rs. 25000.**

questions.question: A and B can together finish a work in 30 days. They worked together for 20 days and then B left. After another 20 days, A finished the remaining work. In how many days can A alone finish the whole work?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

A and B together finish work in 30 days

Worked together for 20 days, then B left

A worked for another 20 days

**Concept: **

If A and B together finish work in 'a' days, A finishes alone in 'b' days and B finishes alone in 'c' days, then 1/a = 1/b + 1/c.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total work done by A and B in 20 days = 20/30 = 2/3 of the work

⇒ Work done by A in the next 20 days = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the work

⇒ Therefore, A alone can finish the work in 20 × 3 = 60 days.

**Hence, A alone can finish the whole work in 60 days.**

questions.question: By selling goods for ₹15,000, Ramu gains ₹3,000. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Selling price = ₹15,000

Profit = ₹3,000

**Concept: **Profit percent = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Cost Price = Selling Price - Profit = ₹15,000 - ₹3,000 = ₹12,000

⇒ Profit percentage = (₹3,000 / ₹12,000) x 100

**Hence, his profit percentage is 25%.**

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a piece of work in 40/3 days. All three started working at it together and after 5 days A left. Then B and C together completed the remaining work in 17 days. Find the number of days (approximately) in which A alone can complete the total work.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A, B and C together can complete a piece of work in 40/3 days

All the three started working at it together and after 5 days A left. Then B and C together completed the work in 17 more days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Let a , b and c be the efficiencies of A , B and C respectively

According to the question,

(a + b + c) × 40/3 days = (a + b + c) × 5 days + ( b + c) × 17 days

40/3a + 40/3b + 40/3c = 5a + 5b + 5c + 17b + 17c

40/3a + 40/3b + 40/3c = 5a + 22b + 22c 

25/3a = 26/3b + 26/3c

25/3a = 26/3(b + c)

25a = 26(b + c)

Ratio of a : (b + c) is 26 : 25

Let 25 and 26 be the efficiency of A and (B+C) 

Total work = (a + b + c) × 40/3 days

= (25 + 26) × 40/3 days

= 51 × 40/3

= 680

Time taken to finish the work by A alone,

= 680/26 = 26 days (approx..)

** ∴ A alone can complete the total work in​ 26 days.**

questions.question: Find the remainder when the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 12, 15 and 25 is divided by 9.
questions.solution:
**Given values:** A number divisible by 12, 15, and 25

**Concept: **

The number is the least common multiple (LCM) of 12, 15, and 25. The remainder when a number is divided by 9 is the same as the remainder when the sum of its digits is divided by 9.

**Calculation:**

⇒ The LCM of 12, 15, and 25 is 300. The smallest 6-digit number divisible by 300 is 100200.

⇒ Sum of digits of 100200 = 1 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 0 + 0 = 3

⇒ Remainder when 3 is divided by 9 = 3

**Therefore, the remainder when the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 12, 15, and 25 is divided by 9 is 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** LCM of 12, 15 and 25 is = 300.

and

300 × 334 = 100200

So, the smallest 6-digit number which is divisible by 12, 15 and 25 is = 100200

When 100200 is divided by 9 then the remainder is:

100200 = 9 × 11133 + 3

remainder is = 3.

questions.question: A train travels from Delhi to Dehradun at the speed of 120 km/h and from Dehradun to Delhi at the speed of 130 km/h. What is the average speed during the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Speed from Delhi to Dehradun = 120 km/h

Speed from Dehradun to Delhi = 130 km/h

**Concept: **

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ If we assume the distance between Delhi and Dehradun to be d km, then total distance = 2d

⇒ Time taken from Delhi to Dehradun = d / 120, and from Dehradun to Delhi = d / 130

⇒ Therefore, average speed = 2d / ((d / 120) + (d / 130))

**Hence, the average speed during the whole journey is approximately 124.8 km/h.**

questions.question: The marked price of a bedsheet is 14 percent more than its cost price. If a discount of 14 percent is given on the marked price. What is the gain or loss percent?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Marked price is 14% more than cost price

Discount of 14% is given on the marked price

**Concept:**

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount, Gain/Loss% = ((Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ If we assume the cost price to be 100 units, then marked price = 114 units

⇒ Selling price = 114 - (14% of 114) = 98.04 units

⇒ Gain or loss percent = ((98.04 - 100) / 100) × 100

**Therefore, there is a 1.96 percent loss.**

questions.question: 75% of first number is equal to 60% of second number. What is the ratio of the first number and second number?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

75% of the first number is equal to 60% of the second number

**Concept: **

Ratio of the first number to the second number is inverse of the ratio of given percentages.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Ratio of the first number to the second number = 60% / 75%

**Therefore, the ratio of the first number to the second number is 4 : 5.**

questions.question: Find the mean proportional between 18 and 32.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

⇒ Mean proportional = √(18 × 32)

⇒ Mean proportional = √(576)

⇒ 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 18

Second number (b) = 32

**Formula Used:**

If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a : x :: x : b, which implies x² = a × b.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58b4c1df84a4bad1e5502c93be4e313cc4976d29d5eb2b69d0f487dffb026a50.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the mean proportional be x.

⇒ x² = 18 × 32

⇒ x² = 576

⇒ x = √576

⇒ x = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies a : b :: b : c. It is calculated using the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b :: c : d. It is calculated using the formula d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Compound Ratio

For ratios a : b and c : d, the compound ratio is the ratio of the product of antecedents to the product of consequents, represented as (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: An almirah was brought for Rs. 14,360 and Rs. 240 was spent on its transportation. At what price should it be sold, to gain 15%?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Cost price of the almirah = Rs. 14,360

Transportation cost = Rs. 240

**Concept: **

Selling price for a gain of p% = Cost price × (1 + p/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total cost price = Rs. 14,360 + Rs. 240 = Rs. 14,600

⇒ Selling price for a gain of 15% = Rs. 14,600 × (1 + 15/100)

**Hence, the almirah should be sold for Rs. 16,790 to gain 15%.**

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 1080 km in 240 minutes. What is the speed of the car in m/sec?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Distance covered = 1080 km

Time taken = 240 minutes

**Concept: **

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance in meters = 1080 × 1000 = 1080000 meters

⇒ Time in seconds = 240 × 60 = 14400 seconds

⇒ Speed = Distance / Time = 1080000 / 14400

**Therefore, the speed of the car is 75 m/sec.**

questions.question: Om decided to order 12 percent more millet flour for his bakery than last year. If he ordered 240 kg last year, then how much quantity of millet flour should he order this year?
questions.solution:
**Given values:**

Last year's order = 240 kg

Increase in order = 12%

**Concept:** Quantity ordered this year = Last year's order × (1 + Increase percentage/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Quantity ordered this year = 240 × (1 + 12/100)

**Therefore, Om should order 268.8 kg of millet flour this year.**
